h1: Maternity Leave Residency Scheduling Without the Headache
paragraph: Stop manually rebuilding schedules for maternity leave. Submit your rules and Scheduling Wizard delivers a fully optimized, ACGME-compliant schedule.

cta.title: Stop Rebuilding Schedules Around Leave
cta.description: Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices who trust Scheduling Wizard to deliver compliant, optimized schedules. Finished schedules in your format, with redrafts through the year included.

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard re-optimizes your affected schedules when a resident goes on maternity leave. You submit the updated rules (including the leave details, duration, and any coverage preferences) and our team redistributes rotations, call assignments, and clinic coverage across your remaining residents. The output is a revised, ACGME-compliant Excel schedule ready to publish, without your team manually rebuilding anything from scratch.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle maternity leave in a residency program?

faq.answer: Yes. Our team enforces ACGME duty hour rules mathematically at the point of schedule generation, not as a manual check afterward. Even when coverage is thinner due to leave, our team will not produce a schedule that violates 80-hour weekly limits, required rest intervals, or subspecialty-specific rules. If a compliant schedule is not achievable under the submitted rules, that conflict is surfaced before delivery.
faq.question: Will ACGME compliance be maintained when a resident is on maternity leave?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard uses algorithmic fairness optimization to redistribute call, weekend, and holiday burden across the remaining residents when someone is on maternity leave. Rather than manually assigning extra shifts to whoever is available, our team balances the additional load equitably across the cohort, minimizing any single resident's disproportionate burden.
faq.question: How do you ensure fair call distribution when one resident is on leave?

faq.answer: Maternity leave typically creates downstream changes across block rotations, call schedules, clinic assignments, and sometimes attending schedules. Scheduling Wizard optimizes all of these simultaneously. Because our team resolves cross-schedule dependencies together, a change in call coverage propagates correctly into rotation and clinic schedules rather than creating new conflicts downstream.
faq.question: What schedule types are affected by maternity leave and does SW handle all of them?

faq.answer: Programs submit their scheduling rules, rotation requirements, ACGME rules, resident preferences, coverage minimums, and the specifics of the maternity leave (dates, affected resident, any accommodation requirements). Scheduling Wizard handles the optimization from there and delivers finished Excel files your team can upload directly to whatever platform you already use.
faq.question: What does the program need to submit to get a revised schedule?

faq.answer: Manual scheduling in Excel requires someone, typically a chief resident, to hand-check every affected rotation, call slot, and clinic assignment for conflicts and compliance after each change. Scheduling Wizard replaces that process entirely. Our team handles all rule checking and redistribution automatically, and institutional scheduling knowledge persists with Scheduling Wizard year over year, so a new chief does not have to relearn how your program's rules work.
